title: Information measures for the EU Cohesion policy for 2022
description: Expected Impact: For the general public: increased public awareness of the results of Cohesion policy and their impact on citizens' lives to Europeans who are unaware of the EU and of the EU action in their region. Information should focus on developing greater understanding of the contribution of Cohesion policy to boosting jobs and growth in Europe and reducing disparities among Member States and regions. For stakeholders: enhanced stakeholders’ engagement (including national, regional and local authorities, beneficiaries, businesses, academia) enabling them to further communicate the impact of Cohesion policy on their regions and to feed into the discussion on the future of Cohesion policy and, more broadly, the future of Europe. Expected Outcome: increased media coverage on Cohesion policy, in particular at regional level enhanced people's awareness of the results of Cohesion policy and their impact on their lives outputs and deliverables such as TV and radio broadcast, online or print coverage, other type of information measures and dissemination - taking multilingualism into account. Objective: The main aim of the call is to provide support for the production and dissemination of information and content linked to EU Cohesion policy, including inter alia the Just Transition Fund, or relevant support under the Recovery Plan for Europe or from the Technical Support Instrument. The proposals should provide coherent, objective and comprehensive information, in order to give an accurate overall picture of the EU Cohesion policy. The proposals should illustrate and assess the role of Cohesion policy in delivering the EU’s political priorities and in addressing current and future challenges for the EU, its Member States, its regions and the local level. Scope: The geographical scope of this call is focussed on EU Member States, including overseas countries and territories (OCTs). The information measures should include one or several activities such as: production and distribution of print, multimedia or audiovisual material web and social media outreach activities media events conferences, seminars, workshops.

title: Access to commercial services through the EOSC hub
description: Instructions for researchers wishing to participate:- Identify the OCRE cloud suppliers in your country using the Cloud Catalogue - https://www.ocre-project.eu/services/cloud-suppliers . Reach out to the contact/s listed for the supplier/s most likely to meet your needs. Collaborate with your supplier on the submission of a proposal which – Clearly highlights your research in terms of discipline and relevance. Describes how your project can demonstrate the significant impact that cloud-based digital services will have on the related activities and outcomes. Shows how your research institute, department and project could tell a compelling story about digital services accelerating European research. Your supplier will require that your institute is prepared to sign their various T&C’s etc should your project be awarded the funded services. Please engage with your procurement and legal team and have them on board. THINK BIG!!! OCRE funded services at this scale could dramatically influence your research outputs this year.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: OCRE is delighted to announce the call to engage in the OCRE EC Funded Cloud Adoption mini competition for the OCRE Framework holders within the EU & UK lots of the OCRE Framework. **** GÉANT invites you to engage with an OCRE Cloud Framework holder in your country for a proposal and compete within the EU & UK lots of the OCRE Framework for the opportunity to get EC Cloud adoption funding awarded to your research project. This mini-competition will provide all OCRE Cloud Framework holders within these lots/countries with an opportunity to get local research project(s) awarded through a ranking of all submitted proposals based on the procedure described below, up to the budget ceiling of the EC Cloud Adoption fund. All proposals will be evaluated, scored, and ranked based on the described awarding criteria (below) after fulfilling the project- and minimum requirements. OCRE Cloud Framework holders can submit their proposal within their awarded EU & UK lots of the Framework and can be awarded maximum of EUR € 500.000,00 (excl. VAT) each of OCRE adoption funding in total. The proposal must describe research project(s) from within the OCRE R&E community of participating institutions, wherein the adoption and benefits of cloud services will be demonstrated. Bids and supporting documents must be in English. Financial Contribution The OCRE adoption funding programme will offer supplier/ researcher collaborations up to a maximum € 500.000,00 (excl. VAT). The research projects must be able to demonstrate significant benefits in terms of the adoption of cloud-based services on their activities and outcomes. Disclaimer: - Due to EU VAT & Voucher Directives this Tender does not cover the countries / lots outside of the EU or UK. In the first call, institutes outside of this region were able to consume awarded services for project collaborations with institutes inside the EU. If you are working within such a research collaboration, please encourage your counterparts in the EU to assist with the submission of a compelling proposal. Research projects spanning more than one country have a good chance of being awarded digital services through OCRE. Projects already consuming these services at scale, or receiving similar funding, will not be considered in the awarding process. It is imperative that this initiative drives the adoption of cloud-based digital services. Awarding criteria Where a OCRE Cloud Framework holder is assessed as passing all Minimum Requirements, the Awarding Criteria will be evaluated and scored. Bidders’ responses to the Awarding Criteria will be assessed as described below and score the for each question weighted in accordance with the values below - Awarding Criterium Description Weight (%) 1 Demonstrating the adoption and benefits of Cloud 40% 2 The project plan 20% 3 Sustainability 20% 4 Best value for money 20% Impact : AC 1: Demonstrating the adoption and benefits of Cloud In Chapter 1 of the tender, the EC principles, Goals of the tender, Project and Institution are described. Your (OCRE Cloud Framework holder/institute) proposal will be assessed and scored on the described added value of the Project to the purpose, how well your proposed Project demonstrates the adoption of Cloud Services. The following Awarding Criteria are applicable: a) Please describe Adoption of Cloud Services: Detail how your proposed project will stimulate the adoption of Cloud Services for other Projects and Institutions; b) Please explain why your proposed project make a good case study on the benefits of using commercial cloud and digital services for research and attract the attention of the broader research community; c) Demonstrate how the specific research project experiences benefits from using the principles (e.g. elasticity) of the cloud. So, what does the project gain by using cloud. Describe benefits in areas like, for example: 1. architecture 2. security 3. collaboration with SME and other project participants (if applicable) 4. duration of the project (architecture, running computations and data correlation) d) Detail how the services of the OCRE Cloud Framework holder embrace and support the adoption of Cloud Services as per the researcher needs and delivers good user experience. AC 4: Best value for money Please describe how the OCRE Cloud Framework holder contribute and will use the EC funded budget to make sure the researcher(s) develop the right skills to work with the Cloud Services and how the collaboration will ensure you stay up to date regarding the possibilities/added value of Cloud services. Implementation (quality and efficiency) : AC 2: The project plan Describe your project plan. How is the successful and timely outcome of the research project with amongst others Professional Support services, IaaS+ resources and (governance) tooling. Describe the roles and responsibilities, risks identified and mitigation which will be taken to minimize them. AC 3: Sustainability The tender aims to fund projects where outcomes (shared through the use cases) aid other projects, researchers, research groups and/or institutions in their understanding of the value that cloud services have for research. Describe the sustainability of the project and added value it creates on the long term. How will the use case of this project aid other research projects in their consideration of cloud services in future projects? Demonstrate which of the cloud functionalities (e.g. advanced Machine Learning) are used and which would not (or much less effective) have been possible using traditional infrastructures. Evaluators: The applications will be evaluated by the OCRE funding team under the oversight of the OCRE External Advisory Board (EAB), experts with insights into European research activities who have no conflict of interest. Minimum requirements and word limit for applications All minimum requirements that should be met for submitting the proposal successfully by the OCRE Cloud Framework holder are stated on the Negometrix procurement platform, on which the OCRE Cloud Framework holders(s) are invited and registered. The word limit for each of the answers on the OCRE Cloud Framework holder’s proposal will also be guided on the Negometrix procurement portal.
furtherInformation:
Who can apply?

All OCRE Cloud Framework holders who were awarded OCRE Framework contracts in the EU/UK lots in the 2020 tender process (www.ocre-project.eu/services/cloud-suppliers). The OCRE Cloud Framework holders are required to collaborate with research institutes in their countries to develop proposals describing compelling research projects which could demonstrate the significant benefits that commercial digital services bring to the researcher. These research projects could be awarded up to € 500,000.00 worth of digital services and consulting from the OCRE Cloud Framework holder.  

Criteria and conditions

  1. The OCRE Cloud Framework holder (supplier) confirms to be able to issue Single Purpose Vouchers (SVP) in accordance with Council Directive (EU) 2016/1065 of 27 June 2016 amending Directive 2006/112/EC / HMRC VAT Notice 741A (14) issued 31 December 2020 regards the treatment of vouchers and stipulations as specified in the tender. OCRE Cloud Framework holder will accept those as a means of payment meeting the minimum criteria. 
  2. The OCRE Cloud Framework holder confirms to be able to treat the issuing; the invoicing; and the VAT treatment, as regards the treatment of vouchers in accordance with Council Directive (EU) 2016/1065 of 27 June 2016 amending Directive 2006/112/EC resp. the UK HMRC VAT Notice 741A (14) issued 31 December 2020. For this contract the VAT will be issued in the country of consumption.
  3. The use of services offered by the OCRE Cloud Framework holder to the Institute are governed by the GEANT OCRE Framework agreement, including the Call-Off Contract. Both the GEANT OCRE framework agreement and the Call-Off Contract are already in the possession of the OCRE Cloud Framework holder and Institution(s) and signed conditionally. This means that if the OCRE Cloud Framework holder is awarded through the mini-competition, the Call Off Contract will enter into force between the Bidder and Institution(s) immediately after the standstill of the tender award notice.
  4. OCRE Cloud Framework holder(s) shall act fully compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
  5. Institutions confirm to be able to provide "on time & in full" the use case information on the project for the EC report 4th of November 2022 the latest.


Further conditions

All other conditions pertain specifically to the OCRE Cloud Framework holder and are described in the actual tender on the Negometrix platform to which all eligible OCRE Cloud Framework holder(s) have been invited to accept. 

Background

The European Commission is determined to make this Europe's digital decade. The EU’s digital strategy will empower people with a new generation of technologies.

Europe must strengthen its digital sovereignty and set standards, rather than following those of others – with a clear focus on data, technology, and infrastructure.

High-quality science, knowledge and innovation accelerate all aspects of the digital and industrial transformations and will bring us closer to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

All OCRE Cloud Framework holder(s) awarded within the EU + UK lots are invited to find Cloud adoption research projects within the R&E community. These Cloud adoption projects should demonstrate proposed benefits from using the Cloud for the specific Institutions of represented R&E community, stimulating above principles.

A OCRE Cloud Framework holder can submit a maximum of one proposal per awarded lot within the EU and UK. If the OCRE Cloud Framework holder submits more proposals, GÉANT reserves the right to put all of the OCRE Cloud Framework holder ’s proposal(s) aside and ignore them.

More Information

For further information please consult the OCRE website: https://www.ocre-project.eu/funding-opportunities/ocre-funding-and-procurement-call
